on_tap.text: Does an East vs West trip swing home court? (time zone travel and body clock)
on_tap.name: Steven

tested.q: In a shootout, every yardage over hits
tested.stat: In 60+ point games, QBs threw 36 yards over projection, WR1s averaged 92 receiving yards (69 otherwise), and RBs gained only 4 rushing yards over. A leg set 10 yards under projection hit 74% for QBs, 65% for WRs, 59% for RBs. But before kickoff, high posted totals show no edge: the same leg hits 53 to 59% at every total.
tested.why: Shootouts are mostly hindsight. Only 15% of games reach 60, about 30% even with a 50+ total, and projections already use the expected points.
tested.bet: Passing and receiving legs gain the most when a game blows up; rushing gains least, so give backs the most cushion. A high total alone is not a reason to load up.

tested.q: Big underdogs get garbage-time backdoor covers
tested.stat: 4.8% backdoor covers: 30 of 619 teams down 17+ after 3 quarters and not covering came back to cover. Within 3 of covering: about 50%. 14+ short: 2%.
tested.why: Trailing teams only outscore the leader by about 1.4 in the 4th. The leader still scores about 5, and both sides rest starters.
tested.bet: No garbage-time bonus on a big dog pregame. Live, a trailing team within 3 of the number entering the 4th is close to a coin flip.

tested.q: Some teams always rally late, some always fold
tested.stat: A team's 4th quarter scoring when down 17+ repeats at 0.05 within a season (odd vs even games) and -0.02 season to season. Leaders resting their defense: -0.05 and 0.16.
tested.why: Teams land in blowouts about twice a season, and one possession swings a 4th quarter by 7. It is luck, not character.
tested.bet: Ignore a team's late-rally reputation; the game situation is what matters.

tested.q: Down two scores, teams sling it
tested.stat: Down 9 to 16 after 3 quarters: 77% passes, 19.3 plays and 7.3 points in the 4th, the most of any margin. Backup QB played in only 14%.
tested.why: The game still looks winnable, so starters stay in and the leader runs 60% of the time to drain the clock.
tested.bet: Live team totals and passing props for a two-score trailer get a volume boost. The full game total does not: close games score 13.4 in the 4th, two-score games 13.1.

tested.q: In a blowout, why risk the starters?
tested.stat: 4th quarters decided by 17+: backup QB threw a pass for 28% of leaders and 29% of trailers, vs 7% in close games. Leaders run 68% of plays.
tested.why: Both coaches protect starters once it is out of reach, so the two effects mostly cancel.
tested.bet: Blowout 4th quarters are the lowest scoring (11.7 total). Don't expect a late scoring burst.

tested.q: A deficit built on turnovers will bounce back
tested.stat: Down 14+ in the 1st half: teams with 2+ more turnovers beat their pregame expectation by +0.3 the rest of the way, vs +2.3 for other deficits. Live win odds (about 12%) matched actual wins (about 11%).
tested.why: Turnovers often come from pressure or forcing throws, and a big lead lets the leader shorten the game either way.
tested.bet: The live line already prices a turnover hole correctly. No bounce-back discount.

tested.q: Three turnovers is FG, FG, TD
tested.stat: Opponents scored 9.5 points on average off a team's first three turnovers. 21 points: 4.1%. Zero: 7.4%. 22+: once (TB vs JAX, 2019).
tested.why: Each turnover costs about 4.3 expected points, but only about 3 get scored directly: 26% next-drive TD, 20% FG, 9% return TD.
tested.bet: Thirteen points is the true cost of three giveaways; about 9 is what the other team actually puts up.

tested.q: Teams should always go for 2
tested.stat: Two-point tries good 47.7% (0.95 points) vs extra points 94.4% (0.94 points). Injury notes: 0.98% of two-point tries vs 0.16% of kicks.
tested.why: On points it is a dead heat. A full goal-line snap carries about 6 times the injury risk of a kick, and runs are rougher than passes.
tested.bet: Teams that go for 2 often make final margins swing more, which matters on spreads near 1, 2, 4 or 8.

tested.q: Teams wear down from heavy workloads
tested.stat: Last week's snaps: about 0.65 points of spread per 10 extra snaps (in Gridline). Snaps over 3 games, 4 games, the whole season, and late-season fading all added nothing.
tested.why: Fatigue is a one-week effect. By the week after, teams have recovered.
tested.bet: A team coming off an 80-snap game is a bit worse this week, and the effect is gone after that.

tested.q: Rain and snow mean unders
tested.stat: Unders hit 64.5% in rain or snow (152 games) and 75% with wind of 10+ too (64 games). Snow alone: about 1 point under.
tested.why: Wet balls and footing slow passing offenses. Now part of Gridline's totals model.
tested.bet: Bettors use forecasts, not actual kickoff weather, so expect less than these numbers.

tested.q: Wind kills scoring
tested.stat: Unders hit 55% at 10 to 14 mph and 56% at 15 to 19 mph. Wind of 15+ costs a QB about 20 passing yards and each receiver about 3.5.
tested.why: It hits the passing game. Rushing barely moves.
tested.bet: Use sustained wind, not gusts. Under 10 mph it doesn't matter.

tested.q: Adrian Hill's crew means unders
tested.stat: Overs 44.7% vs 48.9% league-wide, 1.1 points under the closing total on average, in 114 games since 2015.
tested.why: A lean, but 114 games is within luck, and referee crews added nothing to Gridline's model.
tested.bet: A note, not an edge.

tested.q: Teams that give leads back keep doing it
tested.stat: A team's 2nd half vs expected when leading at the half repeats at 0.13 (odd vs even spots) and 0.06 season to season. The worst third covered 48.7% next time; best third 51.0%.
tested.why: The giving-back didn't continue: those teams were actually +0.3 in their next 2nd half.
tested.bet: Don't fade a favorite for blowing a lead last week.

tested.q: Teams that get blown out keep getting blown out
tested.stat: Flagged teams (2 of last 5 or 3+ this season lost by 17+) got blown out again 19.3% of the time vs 11.3%, but covered 49.3%.
tested.why: It's real, but the lines already know.
tested.bet: No edge on the spread. One unproven lean: flagged teams as 6.5+ point dogs covered 46%.

tested.q: Teams out of the race don't come back
tested.stat: Teams at .300 or worse from week 10 on went 0 for 162 on comebacks from 17+ down in the 2nd half.
tested.why: Season standing is the motivation signal that shows up. A coach's own urgency habit did not predict comebacks.
tested.bet: Down big and out of it means done. Live moneylines on them are long shots for a reason.

tested.q: The team with the better record covers
tested.stat: Better-record team covered 49.9%; with a .400+ win percentage gap, 48.7%; as an underdog, 51.1%.
tested.why: Records are already in the line. Record gap tracked the Vegas line at 0.73.
tested.bet: Records tell you nothing the spread doesn't.

tested.q: A team that covers early keeps covering
tested.stat: A team's weeks 1 to 6 record against the spread vs the rest of its season: correlation -0.03.
tested.why: Lines adjust. Early-season covers are mostly the market catching up.
tested.bet: Don't chase a 5-1 ATS team.

tested.q: Teams on an over streak keep going over
tested.stat: Teams at 80%+ overs early went 44% overs afterward (31 teams). Teams at 20% or less went 55% (43 teams).
tested.why: Totals move up after an over streak, so the streak tends to flip.
tested.bet: If anything, lean the other way, and only lightly.

tested.q: Home field is worth 3 points
tested.stat: Gridline estimates 2.37 since 2021 (raw about 2.0). Vegas home lines average 1.65 and home teams covered 49.3%. Team-specific home edges repeat at 0.02.
tested.why: Smaller than the old 3, and the same for every team.
tested.bet: A team's great home record is not an edge.

tested.q: Only major injuries like a QB or RB matter
tested.stat: Per starter out, in spread points: QB the biggest by far (backup flag about 2, plus the rating drop), WR or TE 1.2, LB 1.3, RB 0.5, D-line or DB 0.3, O-line 0.1.
tested.why: QBs dominate, and RB backups get most of the same yards. The market prices injuries quickly: a model with no injury inputs did as well.
tested.bet: An injury you have read about is already in the number. The edge is timing, or props and college lines that adjust slower.

tested.q: Bye weeks and short weeks decide games
tested.stat: Bye weeks, short weeks, and coming off a division game, shootout or overtime all left Gridline no better or worse.
tested.why: Last week's snap count captures fatigue better than any calendar label.
tested.bet: Rest is already in the line.
